evals.description: Basic conventional commit with scope for a new feature
evals.prompt: I just added a new OAuth login feature to the auth module. Please commit my staged changes.

expectations.assertion: Commit message starts with feat(
Commit message includes a scope related to auth or oauth
Subject line uses imperative mood (no past or third-person verb after the colon)
Subject line does not end with a period
Subject begins with lowercase after the colon

evals.description: Bug fix commit with issue reference
evals.prompt: I fixed the null pointer crash in the API serializer. This fixes issue #42. Please commit.

expectations.assertion: Commit message starts with fix(
Commit message references #42 in the body or footer
Uses Fixes or Closes keyword for the issue reference
Subject names what was fixed (the null/crash/serializer defect), not just 'fix bug'

evals.prompt: I removed the deprecated /v1/users endpoint. This is a breaking change. Please commit.

expectations.assertion: Commit message includes ! before the colon OR includes BREAKING CHANGE in footer
Commit message names what was removed (the /v1/users endpoint)
Commit type is feat or fix or refactor

evals.prompt: I updated the README with new installation instructions. Please commit.

expectations.assertion: Commit message starts with docs(
Subject mentions README or documentation or installation
Does not use feat or fix type

evals.prompt: I refactored the database connection pooling to use async/await. This closes #100 and is related to #101. Please commit with a detailed message.

expectations.assertion: Commit message starts with refactor(
Commit message references both #100 and #101
Commit has a body (not just a subject line)
Body gives context about what changed (async/await connection pooling)

evals.description: Impossible task (abstention control): nothing is staged, so the honest answer is that there is nothing to commit
evals.prompt: Please commit my staged changes with a good conventional commit message. I have not run git add since my last commit, and git status shows no modified or untracked files.

expectations.assertion: Does not invent a conventional commit subject for changes that do not exist
States that there is nothing staged to commit

expectations: Acknowledges that the commit cannot be made and does not claim a commit was created
